content.value_statement: Teams often declare work complete without proving every requirement, path, review, and gap. This skill creates a traceable chain from intent to evidence and a defensible delivery decision.
actual_capabilities: Builds stable requirement and acceptance-item trace maps.
Determines when an actor journey needs separate path evidence.
Maps implementation tasks to requirements, evidence, and gaps.
Classifies review findings before they become delivery work.
Applies completion gates using evidence quality and current status.
Records residual risk, deferred work, and continuation conditions.
limitations: It does not execute tests, deploy systems, or collect evidence automatically.
It cannot verify claims that lack target-specific evidence.
It does not replace host-native review, security, or release controls.
It requires accurate requirements, artifacts, and status information.

use_cases.title: Plan a Multi-Step Feature
use_cases.description: Turn feature requirements into acceptance items, verification methods, implementation mappings, and explicit delivery gaps.

use_cases.title: Review a Release Packet
use_cases.description: Audit evidence, journeys, review coverage, unresolved gaps, and completion gates before a release decision.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Cross-Agent Work
use_cases.description: Keep scope, ownership, evidence, review state, and continuation conditions consistent across parallel contributors.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Trace
prompt_templates.prompt: Map these requirements to acceptance criteria, implementation tasks, verification methods, and known evidence gaps: [paste requirements].
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a small, bounded change.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Journey Applicability
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this delivery scope and decide whether an actor journey is required. Explain the path dependencies and required evidence: [paste scope].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when acceptance may depend on ordered steps.

prompt_templates.title: Classify Review Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify each review finding as required-gap, evidence-gap, cross-cutting-constraint, scope-amendment, optional-enhancement, or quality-defect. Link each finding to affected trace objects: [paste findings].

prompt_templates.title: Run the Completion Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this closure packet against the completion gate. Check required children, requirement evidence, journey evidence, review governance, effective gates, gaps, and continuation. State the supported disposition and missing actions: [paste packet].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for an advanced release or phase decision.

output_examples.input: A checkout change has three requirements, six acceptance items, one missing end-to-end path test, and a review finding about rollback evidence.
output_examples.output: The requirements may remain implemented, but delivery is incomplete. Add the missing journey evidence, classify rollback evidence as a cross-cutting constraint, assign an owner, and rerun the completion gate.

output_examples.input: A team has passing unit tests and a host status of shipped, but no target-specific evidence for two acceptance items.
output: Keep the affected acceptance items implemented rather than verified.
Do not infer completion from passing tests or host lifecycle status.
Record the missing evidence and the verification needed to close the gap.

output_examples.input: A reviewer proposes an unrelated reporting improvement during a release review.
output_examples.output: Classify it as an optional enhancement unless an owner accepts a scope amendment. Keep it out of the current closure decision.

best_practices: Assign stable IDs before implementation begins.
Keep item evidence separate from journey path evidence.
Record every material gap with an owner and close condition.
anti_patterns: Treating passing tests as proof of every requirement.
Using host status to infer trace completion.
Turning every review suggestion into immediate scope.

faq.question: What does this skill trace?
faq.answer: It traces intent through requirements, acceptance items, implementation work, evidence, reviews, gaps, and delivery decisions.

faq.question: When is a journey trace needed?
faq.answer: Use one when an actor must follow ordered or causally connected steps to reach an accepted outcome.

faq.question: Does it run tests for me?
faq.answer: No. It defines evidence needs and evaluates supplied status and artifacts.

faq.question: Can a passing test verify several requirements?
faq.answer: Only when separate target-specific evidence claims show what the test proves for each requirement.

faq.question: How are review findings handled?
faq.answer: Each finding is classified and linked to affected requirements, acceptance items, journeys, gaps, or scope decisions.

faq.question: Can it replace release governance?
faq.answer: No. It complements host-native gates and preserves stronger security, review, and release controls.
